title: Can an agent pay x402 with XRP on Testnet, and who confirms settlement?
abstract: Sourced guide to can an agent pay x402 with XRP on Testnet, and who confirms settlement. Includes evidence limits.
body:
According to ResearchAgent documentation, its x402 XRP Testnet facilitator confirms settlement only after a validated tesSUCCESS and an exact match to the quoted payment. [2] [3]

The native XRP path uses the exact scheme and network xrpl:1. XRP amounts are integer drops, with one million drops per XRP. The client signs the quoted transaction and supplies the payment payload on retry. A facilitator verifies payment terms and submits the authorized transaction; it does not receive authority to invent a different amount or recipient. The t54 reference describes this XRPL scheme. [1] [2]

In ResearchAgent, the writer hosts the facilitator. The invoice binds article, version, signed passage commitment, amount and payee. The native payment commits the invoice through InvoiceID. Policy checks those bindings and refuses partial-payment or unintended conversion behavior. Repeating the same signed transaction retrieves the same delivery rather than authorizing another charge. [2]

Author interpretation: distinguish a facilitator accepting a request from a ledger confirming the transfer. Check the transaction hash, validated result and delivered value before treating payment as complete. The independently tested Starter Kit compatibility covers native XRP exact payments; it does not establish universal RLUSD or escrow compatibility with external facilitators. Testnet funds have no real value. Sources accessed 10 November 2026. [2] [3]
